title: Oct 3 Results + Oct 4 Preview: Three Straight Wins to Close the Night
summary: Model bounced back strong with 3-1 performance after early stumble in Cleveland

content.value:
## Looking Back at October 3rd

You know, I've been doing this long enough to tell you that a 3-1 night is nothing to sneeze at, especially when you recover from an early miss the way our model did yesterday. The Guardians game didn't go our way—52% confidence turned into a learning moment—but then we rattled off three straight winners. That's the kind of resilience you want to see from any system worth its salt.

## What Worked Yesterday

The Dodgers call at 65% was our strongest conviction, and Atlanta couldn't keep pace in Chavez Ravine. No surprises there—when LA is rolling at home, you ride that wave. The Rays pulled through at 59%, and Milwaukee squeaked past the Padres despite modest 53% confidence. Sometimes the narrow margins are the ones that separate good handicapping from great handicapping.

That Cleveland miss? It happens. 52% is essentially a coin flip with a slight lean, and the Sox showed up when it mattered. I've seen enough baseball to know you can't win 'em all, especially the tight ones.

## Tomorrow's Slate: October 4th

Here's where it gets interesting. We're going right back to the well with Milwaukee against San Diego. Same matchup, same venue, but this time we're looking at a different pitching dynamic with Michael King taking the hill for the Padres and Logan Henderson countering for the Brewers.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - October 4th
content.value: Milwaukee Brewers over San Diego Padres
content.sub: 50% confidence · King vs Henderson · American Family Field

content.value:
## The October 4th Analysis

Now, a 50% pick might raise some eyebrows—I can already hear the questions. But here's the thing: when you're at dead even on paper and the model still leans one way, there's usually something underneath worth exploring. Milwaukee just beat this same Padres squad yesterday, and there's value in home momentum that doesn't always show up in the numbers.

Michael King has been solid for San Diego, no question about it. But Logan Henderson at home in Milwaukee, with the crowd behind him and the confidence of a fresh victory? That's a recipe for another tight, well-pitched game that could tilt either direction. We're taking the home nine.

I've been around long enough to know that 50-50 games are where October baseball lives. This is playoff atmosphere stuff, even if we're still in the regular season. Brewers have the slight edge in our system, and sometimes slight is all you need.

## The Veteran's Take

Three-and-one is a winning day in anybody's book. You take those returns, bank the confidence, and move forward. Tomorrow's a new slate, same matchup as yesterday, and we're sticking with what worked: Milwaukee at home. The October grind is all about consistency and conviction, even when the margins are razor-thin.

See you after first pitch.
